title: You’ve felt it before.
paragraphs: You’ve felt it before.
That sudden pull in your chest… the quiet nudge you couldn’t explain… the thought that didn’t sound like your usual thinking.
And for a moment—you wondered…
Was that God?
Or was that just you?
Then you brushed it off. Logic stepped in. Emotion got blamed. And what could have been sacred got reduced to “just a feeling.”
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
You’re not asking a modern question.
You’re standing in an ancient tension.
Because long before your doubt, there were people who heard God and still questioned if it was really Him.
“Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, and the word of the Lord had not yet been revealed to him.” — 1 Samuel 3:7
Samuel heard a voice calling his name… three times.
And each time, he misinterpreted it.
God was speaking.
But Samuel didn’t recognize it yet.
Read that again.

God was speaking…
and the problem wasn’t silence—
it was recognition.
So let’s confront this honestly.
Does God still speak today?
Or are we just interpreting feelings?
You already know the answer isn’t simple—because your experience isn’t.
There are moments that feel too precise to be random.
And there are moments that feel suspiciously like your own desires dressed up as “God’s will.”
So where is the line?
Here’s the truth Scripture refuses to let you ignore:
“Long ago, at many times and in many ways, God spoke… but in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son.” — Hebrews 1:1–2
God is not silent.
But He is not chaotic either.
He has already spoken clearly—through Jesus Christ.
That means this:
If you’re waiting for a voice while ignoring His Word…
you’re not being spiritual.
You’re being selective.
God’s primary voice today is not your feelings.
It’s not impressions.
It’s not vague inner whispers that contradict Scripture.
It is His revealed Word—alive, active, and piercing:
“For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword…” — Hebrews 4:12
So yes… God still speaks.
But not in a way that competes with what He has already said.
And this is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because a lot of what people call “God speaking” is actually this:
Their desires…
Their fears…
Their wounds…
Their assumptions…
filtered through spiritual language.
You knew.
God saw it.
That time you said, “I feel like God is leading me…”
but it conveniently aligned with what you already wanted.
That wasn’t divine revelation.
That was internal permission.
And deep down…
you sensed it.
But here’s where it shifts—because this isn’t about shutting down the supernatural.
It’s about restoring clarity.
Jesus said:
“My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.” — John 10:27
So yes, His people recognize His voice.
But notice what proves it.
Not the feeling.
The following.
Not the impression.
The obedience.
If what you’re “hearing” doesn’t lead you toward repentance…
toward holiness…
toward surrender to Christ…
it’s not His voice.
Because God does not speak in contradiction to His nature.
And His nature is revealed in Jesus.
“Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.” — John 17:17
So now the real question isn’t:
“Is God speaking?”
The real question is:
Are you listening where He has already spoken?
Because you can chase signs, voices, and impressions your whole life…
and still miss Him completely.
Jesus warned about this:
“An evil and adulterous generation seeks for a sign…” — Matthew 12:39
Not because signs are evil…
but because dependence on them can replace surrender to truth.
And this is where everything comes to a breaking point.
Because if God’s voice is clearest in His Word…
then ignoring Scripture while chasing feelings is not spiritual hunger—
it’s resistance.
And now you’re faced with something deeper than confusion.
You’re faced with a decision.
Will you trust your feelings…
or will you trust what God has already said?
Because one will comfort you temporarily.
The other will transform you eternally.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
And here’s the part many avoid:
God has already spoken about your sin.
About your need for repentance.
About the reality of judgment.
And about the only way to be saved.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
“That if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.” — Romans 10:9
That’s not a feeling.
That’s truth.
So if you’re waiting for a mystical experience before you respond to God…
you’re delaying obedience to what He has already made clear.
And time isn’t neutral.
Every delay shapes your heart.
Either softer…
or harder.
But here’s the hope that changes everything:
God is not playing hide and seek with you.
He has revealed Himself fully in Jesus Christ.
Not so you would guess your way to Him…
but so you could know Him.
Not through confusion.
But through truth.
And once you anchor yourself there…
something incredible happens.
Your feelings stop leading.
And your discernment starts forming.
You begin to recognize what aligns with Him…
and what doesn’t.
Not because you’re chasing voices—
but because you know His.
And that changes everything.
Say it plainly.
“I’ve been listening to myself more than God.”
Or…
“I want to hear Him the right way.”
Let it come out.
Because silence won’t heal what truth is trying to confront.
There are people around you right now who are stuck in the same confusion.
Send this to them.
Not as pressure—
but as clarity.
Follow this path if you’re ready to go deeper—because surface-level faith won’t sustain you.
You’ll need to come back to it when your feelings get loud again.
And if you’re ready to grow in real discernment, grounded in Scripture—not emotion, not assumption—step into deeper teaching here:
This isn’t about hearing more voices.
It’s about finally recognizing the One that’s already speaking.
